newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firm, mkts sells long dollars.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firm, mkts sells long dollars.

text.p: The peso reversed its early weakness at the close of trade on Friday to close firmer for the second day in a row.
Dealers said investors sold surplus dollars they had bought in speculative morning trade.
"The market was awash in dollars. I think they went long (dollars) to hedge against further peso weakness," a trader said. "But when that didn't happen, they decided to sell."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed the session 1.4 centavos firmer at 7.9450/7.9470 and 7.9420/7.9450 per dollar, respectively.
Same-day peso contracts did not trade as U.S. financial markets were closed due to the July 4 Independence Day holiday.
Dealers said the peso had weakened in a mild speculative run on the peso ahead of Mexican elections on Sunday.

Mexicans vote on Sunday for a new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time, a mayor of Mexico City. Previously, that post has been filled by a presidential nominee.

The outcome of the mayoral race is critical, because for the first time President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) may lose control of the nerve center of Mexico to an opposition party. The PRI has ruled Mexico for 68 unbroken years.
Several dealers said they expected the peso to open firm on Monday, unless election results contained any surprises.
"I think Monday will be very calm, unless anything extraordinary happens on Sunday (election day)," he said.
